title: Nimble Fermented North Indian Dill Nuka-Pickle Dosa
description: A North Indian-inspired dosa recipe featuring the tangy, crunch of nuka-pickle and the fresh zing of dill, perfect for a weekend brunch.
instructions: Soak the idli rice and split black gram in water for 4 hours.
Grind the soaked rice and gram into a fine paste using a grinder or blender.
Transfer the paste to a large mixing bowl and add the grated ginger, dill leaves, nuka-pickle, salt, and baking soda.
Mix well to combine and adjust the seasoning as needed.
Add the water and mix until the batter is smooth and free of lumps.
Rest the batter for 2 hours to allow the fermentation to begin.
Heat a non-stick dosa pan or griddle over medium heat.
Spread a small ladle of the batter onto the pan and tilt to evenly coat the surface.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until the bottom is golden brown, then flip and cook for another minute.
Repeat with the remaining batter to make 8-10 dosas.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
